heroHeadline: Sept 16: SPCX Slips to ~$143.51 as Musk Won't Rule Out Tesla Merger, Valor Distributes $8.5B; Vandenberg Launch Scrub
heroSubtitle: 8,899 days since SpaceX founding — SPCX shares traded around $143.51 on Sept 16 (day range $142.87-$148.54), down from Sept 15's close of $148.15, after Elon Musk declined to rule out a future Tesla-SpaceX merger at the Sept 15 All-In Summit ("With all this collaboration, on so many levels, who can imagine what action one might take"); Jefferies and JPMorgan both flagged strategic logic in a combination, and Kalshi priced the odds of a merger before 2028 at 66%, though no formal proposal exists. Separately, longtime backer Valor Equity Partners (Antonio Gracias) disclosed distributing about $8.5 billion of SpaceX stock — roughly 8.5% of its holdings — to limited partners, its biggest-ever investment win and first distribution since the June 2026 IPO. On the launch side, SpaceX scrubbed the Falcon 9 launch of the classified USSF-259 mission for U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg SLC-4E prior to fueling Sept 15, with a backup attempt targeted for Sept 16. Starship Flight 14's target has slipped again, from Sept 18 to no earlier than Sept 22, as Booster 21 and Ship 41 remain in final Starbase checkout.
